newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Prisoners riot in north Tajikistan, hold hostages.
newsitem.headline: Prisoners riot in north Tajikistan, hold hostages.

text.p: Tajikistan's Interior Minister said on Wednesday that prisoners were rioting in a labour camp in the north of the former Soviet republic and local police said they were holding two guards hostage.
"The riots started yesterday," Interior Minister Homiddin Sharipov told Reuters in the capital Dushanbe. It was unclear what the prisoners, in the city of Khudjand, were demanding.

Khudjand police said by telephone that the prison held between 700 and 800 inmates and that two prison officers were being held captive. But neither the police nor the minister gave details of any casualties.
Official sources in Dushanbe said a unit of elite troops had flown to Khudjand and a local official said he had seen armoured personnel carriers driving up to the prison.
However, Sharipov said: "We will negotiate with the prisoners".
Prison conditions around central Asia are poor. Bloody rioting hit a prison in Turkmenistan last year while tuberculousis is rife in Kazakh prisons.
Tajikistan is a mountainous country bordering Afghanistan and China and is trying to emerge from a bitter civil war.
